llm.summary: This fact-checking skill is a disclosed wrapper around Cue’s external research service, with privacy considerations users should notice before sending sensitive material.

dimensions.detail: The required git, python3, curl, network access, Cue API key, and report output file are proportionate for an external fact-checking integration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact itself is only SKILL.md and contains no executable installer, while the text refers to a bundled one-click install script with an empty command block and relies on an external runner path under ~/.cue.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly says the flow is Agent to Cue API to external data sources, but the invocation section does not put a prominent warning next to the command that submitted text may leave the local machine.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill reads a Cue API key from ~/.cue/config.json or the environment and writes reports under ~/cue-reports; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no evidence of privilege escalation, destructive actions, or hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is fact-checking via source cross-checking and data review, and the runtime instructions align with that purpose by sending a user-supplied query to Cue using a fixed fact-check template and returning a structured report.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending the material you ask it to check to Cue and its external research workflow. Avoid submitting confidential reports, non-public allegations, client data, or regulated personal information unless your organization has approved Cue for that use. Review the external runner before installing because it is not bundled in this submitted artifact.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The concern is partially supported because sensitive due-diligence or report text could be submitted, and the command section does not repeat a privacy warning. It is downgraded to guidance because the architecture section explicitly discloses Cue API and external data source processing, and that data flow is central to the stated fact-checking purpose.
